translations.text: These are the words of this letter, which Baruch son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Seraiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote. He wrote these things to Babylon.
In the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans captured Jerusalem and burned it with fire.
Baruch read these words written in this scroll in the hearing of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who came to listen to this scroll.

And in the hearing of the officials, the king’s officials, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest—all those living in Babylon and along the River Sur.
They wept, fasted, and prayed before the Lord.
Each person gathered money according to what he had at hand and what he could afford.
He sent it to Jerusalem, to Jehoiakim son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, the priest, and to the priests and all the people who were found with him in Jerusalem.

When he took the vessels of the Lord’s house that he had brought out of the temple, to return them to the land of Judah on the tenth day of Nisan—the vessels that Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made.
After King Nebuchadnezzar had taken captive Jeconiah, the officials, the smiths, the craftsmen, and the troops from Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babylon.
They said, “Look, we have sent you money. With the money buy a whole burnt offering for sin and frankincense. Prepare an offering and offer it on the altar of the Lord our God.
Pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and for the life of Belteshazzar his son, so that their days on earth may be like the days of heaven.

May the Lord give us strength to serve him, and may our eyes shine. May we live under the protection of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and Belteshazzar his son, serve them for many days, and find mercy in their sight.
Pray and plead for us with the Lord our God, because we have sinned before the Lord our God, and the fury and anger of the Lord our God have not turned away from us to this very day.
Read this scroll that we have sent you, and make confession on our behalf in the Lord’s house, before the Lord, on the festival day and on the days of the Lord.
Say, ‘Righteousness belongs to the Lord our God, but shame belongs to us, as it does this very day—to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And to our kings and our officials, and to our priests, our prophets, and our ancestors.
We who have sinned before the Lord our God.

We have not listened to him, and we have despised his commandments. We have not obeyed or listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to follow the commandments of the Lord our God that he set before us.
For from the day when the Lord brought our ancestors out of the land of Egypt until this day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God and have rebelled, refusing to listen to his voice.

Disaster and the curse have come upon us—the curse that the Lord commanded Moses his servant to pronounce on the day when he brought our ancestors out of the land of Egypt to give us a land flowing with milk and honey.
We have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to carry out all the words of his servants the prophets whom he sent to us.
Each of us followed the desires of his evil heart, serving foreign gods and doing evil in the sight of the Lord our God.

The Lord fulfilled his words, what he had spoken against us and against our judges who judged Israel and Judah, against our kings and officials, and against the people of the house of Israel and Judah.
The Lord brought great disasters upon us, the like of which had never happened under heaven anywhere on earth, as happened in Jerusalem, just as it is written in the law of Moses.
So that everyone would eat the flesh of his son, and everyone would eat the flesh of his daughter.
He handed them over to all the kingdoms around us, to disgrace and the sword among all the nations around us—us whom the Lord scattered.
We have become lower and lower, not higher and higher, because we have sinned against the Lord our God and have not listened to his voice.
Righteousness belongs to the Lord our God, but shame belongs to us and our ancestors, as it does today.
For the Lord our God pronounced against us all these calamities that he has brought upon us.
Yet we did not ask the Lord that each of us might turn away from the desires of his evil heart.
The Lord kept watch over these disasters and brought them upon us, because the Lord our God is righteous in all his deeds that the Lord commanded us.
We have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to follow the commandments of the Lord that he set before us.

And now, Lord, God of Israel, you are the one who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, with signs and wonders, with great power and an uplifted arm. You made a name for yourself that endures to this day.
We have sinned, done wrong, and acted wickedly, Lord our God, against all your commandments and all your righteousness.
Turn your fury away from us, because only a few of us remain out of many, and we are few among the nations where you have scattered us.’
But hear, Lord, our prayer and our plea. Deliver us for your name’s sake, and grant us mercy in the sight of our captors.
Then the whole earth will know that you are the Lord our God, because your holy name has been invoked over Israel and his descendants.
Look, Lord, and see from your holy dwelling. Look upon us, Lord; incline your ear and hear us.

Open your eyes, Lord, and see. For it is not the dead who have gone down to Sheol, whose spirit has been taken from their inward parts, who will praise the Lord, give him thanks, and acknowledge his righteousness.
Rather, the distressed soul that grieves over its greatness, that walks in humility and sickness, and failing eyes and a hungry soul will praise you and acknowledge your righteousness, Lord.
For we do not rely on our righteousness or on the righteousness of our ancestors and our kings when we seek mercy from you and lay our supplication before you, Lord our God.
For you have turned all your fury and anger against us, just as you spoke through your servants the prophets, saying:
“Bow your shoulders and serve the king of Babylon, and live in the land that I gave your ancestors.
And if you do not obey the Lord’s voice by serving the king of Babylon—”

“I will bring complete destruction upon the cities of Judah and the surroundings of Jerusalem. I will put an end to the sound of rejoicing and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride. The whole land will become a ruin, with no one living in it.”

We did not obey your command to serve the king of Babylon. So you fulfilled the words you spoke through your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our ancestors would be brought out of their resting places and their graves.
Now they lie cast out in the heat by day and in the frost by night. They died in terrible suffering, through devastation, famine, the sword, and captivity.
You made the house over which your name was invoked a ruin, as it is today, because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
Yet you have dealt with us, Lord our God, according to all your kindness, according to all your will, and according to your abundant mercy.
This is just as you spoke through your servant Moses on the day when you commanded him to write your law in the sight of Israel, saying:
“If you do not obey my voice, this great and numerous people will instead become few and dwindle among the nations where I have scattered them.
For I know that they will not obey me, because they are a stubborn people. They will turn their hearts toward the land of their captivity.
They will know that I am the Lord their God, and I will give them an understanding heart and ears with which to hear.
They will praise me in the land of their captivity and remember my name.
They will turn away from their stubbornness and their evil deeds, because they will remember the way of their ancestors, who sinned before the Lord.
I will bring them back to the land that I swore to give their ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they will possess it. I will multiply them, and they will not decrease.
I will establish an everlasting covenant with them. I will be their God, and they will be my people. I will never again remove my people Israel from the land that I gave them.”
Almighty Lord, God of Israel, a soul in distress, a spirit in sorrow, and an afflicted body cry out to you.
Hear, Lord God, and have mercy, for you are merciful and compassionate. Have mercy on us, because we have sinned before you.
For you endure forever, but we perish forever.

Almighty Lord, God of Israel, hear the prayer of those who have died in Israel, and also that of their children who sinned before you and did not obey the voice of the Lord. Curses and calamities have clung to us.
Do not remember the wrongdoing and sins of our ancestors, but remember your hand and your name at this time.
For you are the Lord our God, and they will praise you, Lord.

For this reason you have put fear of you in our hearts, so that we may call upon your holy name and praise you in our captivity. For we have taken to heart all the evil deeds and wrongdoing of our ancestors who sinned before you.

Here we are today in our captivity, where you have scattered us to suffer a curse, disgrace, reproach, and condemnation, in keeping with all the sins and wrongdoing of our ancestors who rebelled against you, Lord our God.
Hear, Israel, the commandment of life. Listen, so that you may learn understanding and wisdom.
Why is it, Israel, that you have grown old in the land of your enemies and become defiled with the dead in a foreign land?
You have also been counted among those who go down to Sheol.
Because you abandoned the fountain of wisdom.
If you had walked in God's way, you would have lived in peace forever and ever.
Learn where wisdom is, where strength is, and where understanding is, so that you may also know where length of days of life is, where life is, and where the light of life and peace are.
Who has found its place, or who has entered its storehouse and treasury?
Where are the rulers of the world and those who exercise dominion over the animals of the earth?
And those who amuse themselves with the birds of heaven, who store up silver for themselves in treasuries, and gold in which people trust—there is no end to their possessions.
Those who acquire silver and concern themselves with it, whose works are beyond counting?
They perished and went down to Sheol, and others arose in their place.
Young men saw the light and lived in the land, but they did not know the way of understanding and wisdom.
They did not understand her paths or hold fast to her. Their children kept themselves far from her way and rebelled.
It was not heard of in Canaan, nor was it seen in Teman.

Nor did the descendants of Hagar, those who seek understanding on earth, the merchants of Morath and Teman, those who tell stories, and those who investigate and seek understanding. They did not know the way of wisdom or reach her paths.
O Israel, how great is the house of the Lord God, and how long and broad is the territory he possesses!
It has no end; it is high and cannot be measured.
There were born the renowned giants of the beginning, who were very great and knew warfare.
God did not choose these, nor did he give them the way of wisdom.
They perished because they had neither wisdom nor understanding. They perished for lack of thought, because they had no discernment.
Who has gone up to heaven, taken hold of it, and brought it down from the clouds?
Or who has crossed the reaches and farthest end of the sea, found it, and brought it back like choice gold?
There is no one who knows its way, nor anyone who understands its paths.
But the one who knows everything knows her; he found her through his wisdom. He established the earth forever and ever and filled it with four-footed animals.
He sends out the light, and it goes; he calls it, and it obeys him and answers him with trembling.
The stars shone in their places and rejoiced.
He calls them, and they say, “Here we are!” They shone joyfully for the one who made them.
This is God, and there is no other besides him; no other is to be reckoned apart from him.
He is the one who found the whole way of wisdom and gave it to Jacob his servant and to Israel his beloved.
After these things, he was revealed and seen on earth, and he lived among human beings.
This is the book recording the commandments of God, and the law that endures forever. For all who hold fast to it, it will be life, but those who abandon them will die.
Turn back and learn, Jacob. Persevere and walk in its way, toward the radiance of its light.
Do not give your glory and honor to another, or what is good and beneficial for you to a foreign people.
We are blessed, and blessed are you, Israel, because we know what is pleasing to our God.
Be comforted, people of God, a memorial for Israel.
For you were sold to the nations, but not for destruction. Rather, because you angered God, you were handed over to your enemies.
For you angered the one who made you, the eternal God, because you sacrificed to demons and not to God.
You forgot the eternal God who raised you, and you also grieved Jerusalem, who nurtured you.
For I saw anger and wrath coming upon you from the Lord, and I said, “Listen to me, inhabitants of Zion, for the Lord God has brought great, everlasting mourning upon me.
For I saw the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Lord of the ages brought upon them.
For I raised them with joy, but I sent them away with weeping, mourning, and sighs.
Let no one rejoice over my widowhood, for I have been abandoned and emptied of my many people because of my children's sins, because they strayed from the way of the Lord God.
They did not know his commandments or his judgments. Nor did they walk in the way of God's commandments, or in the path of true instruction, in righteousness.
Understand, or be persuaded, you inhabitants of Zion. Remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Lord of the ages brought upon them.
For he brought against them a nation from far away, an insolent nation speaking another language. They showed no respect for the elderly and no mercy to the young.
They took captive and carried away the widow’s loved ones and her daughters, and devastated her who was alone and isolated.
For I am unable to help you.
For the very one who brought disaster upon you delivers you from the hands of your enemies.
Go, my children, go! For I have been left ruined and desolate.
I have taken off the robe of peace and put on sackcloth in my supplication. I will cry out to you, the Ever-living One, day after day.
Wake up, my children, and cry out to the Lord, and he will rescue you from the hands of the powerful, from the hands of rulers, and from the hands of enemies.

For I placed my hope for your deliverance in the one who lives forever. Joy came to me from the Lord, the everlasting God, because he soon had mercy on them, because of the compassion of God, their everlasting Savior.
For I sent you away with mourning and weeping, but God will bring you back to me, and I will receive you from him with everlasting joy and delight.

Just as the inhabitants of Zion have now seen your captivity, so they will soon see your deliverance from the Lord our God. He will bring you back with great joy, with praise, and with the light of the Lord of the ages.
My children, be patient and endure the wrath that has come upon you from the Lord God. Your enemy pursued you; therefore you will soon see his destruction, and you will tread on their necks.
My pampered children went into captivity. They traveled the rough roads of [?] and were scattered along difficult paths. They were scattered like a flock snatched away by enemies.
Take comfort, my children, and cry out to the Lord God. For you will be remembered before the Lord by the one who brought these things upon you.
For just as your mind wandered away from the Lord, return with tenfold zeal and turn to the Lord, and seek God.
For the very one who brought calamity upon you will bring you everlasting joy together with your deliverance.”
Take comfort, Jerusalem. The one who gave you your name comforts you.
Let the cities that harmed you and rejoiced over your downfall be afraid.
Let the cities that enslaved your children be alarmed. You will rejoice over their downfall. Let those who harmed you be afraid; let the city that received your children be alarmed.
For just as she rejoiced over your downfall, so she will be distressed and grieve over her own devastation.
I will remove from her the carved images and the jubilation of great crowds, and her joy will turn to mourning.
For fire will be sent upon her from the one who lives forever, for many days, and demons will dwell in her for all time.
Look toward the east, Jerusalem, and see the joy coming to you from God.

For look, your children whom you sent away are coming to you. They are coming and gathering from where the sun rises to where it sets, at the word of the Lord, the holy God, rejoicing in the glory of God.
Jerusalem, take off the robe of your mourning, your misery, and your sorrow. Put on the majesty that comes from the Lord God, for everlasting glory.
Wrap yourself in the cloak of righteousness that comes from God. Place on your head the crown of the glory of the Lord of the ages.
For God himself will show everyone that your light shines over the whole earth.
For God will give you this name forever: “Peace of righteousness and glory of reverence for God.”

Wake up, wake up, Jerusalem! Stand on the [?]. Look toward the east and the west, and see your children gathering to you from where the sun rises to where it sets, at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God remembers them.
For they left you on foot, driven away by the enemy. But God is bringing them back to you, lifted up in glory on a royal throne.

For God has commanded every high mountain to be brought low and every hill to become smooth and level. All the valleys will be filled, and the earth will be made level so that Israel may walk confidently in truth, in the glory of God.
All the trees of the forest and every fragrant tree have spread their shade over Israel at God's command.
For the God of Israel will reign over you with joy and in the light of his glory, with mercy and righteousness that come from our God.
